implementation_statement: Access control policy POL-02 (2024) was revised and approved 2026-09-22, effective 2026-10-01 (P06). It now covers every group company, including acquired companies from closing. The joiner, mover, and leaver procedure and the access review procedure are due 2026-11-30.

Accounts are created in the directory from HRIS hire events and synchronized to the cloud identity provider, which federates to the ERP, HRIS, treasury, loan servicing, distribution, and field-service systems. Gaps: subsidiary terminations reach shared IT on average 2 business days late; transfers between subsidiaries keep prior access (P07: 6 of 25 sampled transfers); only the ERP is reviewed (twice a year); Home Services North users are outside the directory.
evidence: HRIS-to-directory workflow; identity provider export; ERP review records 2026-01 and 2026-07; P07 samples

implementation_statement: Account creation and disablement are automated from HRIS events for integrated entities. Transfers are not automated, and Home Services North is not connected (gap 2).
The identity provider disables accounts with no sign-in for 60 days; a weekly report lists them for the service desk.

Each SaaS system enforces role-based access. Role owners approve assignments: Controller (ERP), Treasurer (treasury system), VP of Human Resources (HRIS), Finance President (loan servicing), subsidiary Presidents (their systems). Cloud access uses provider roles assigned from directory groups.

The cloud hub firewall controls flows between sites and workloads; the SFTP server accepts connections only from the banks and the integration service. Gap: the Fabrication plant floor and office networks are one flat network (gap 9).
evidence: Hub firewall rules; plant network diagram

implementation_statement: ERP roles separate vendor master changes from payment release; the treasury system requires a second approver for every wire and ACH batch; bank dual approval is enforced by the banks.
evidence: ERP segregation of duties matrix; treasury approval rules

implementation_statement: Least privilege applies to SaaS roles and cloud roles. Gaps: 14 Domain Admins members including 4 service accounts; 6 standing global administrators in the identity provider; HR collaboration site with plan PHI open to 11 HR staff instead of 2 (gap 6); 96 collaboration sites never reviewed.
evidence: Directory group export; identity provider role export; site permission report

implementation_statement: Security functions (EDR policy, SIEM, cloud guardrails) are limited to the security team and the MSSP. Directory security settings are still changeable by all Domain Admins.
Administrators have separate admin accounts for the cloud consoles and identity provider. Directory administration is still done with everyday accounts by 3 of 9 directory administrators.
Cloud console privileges use just-in-time elevation through the privileged access broker. Directory, identity provider, ERP, and treasury administrators hold standing rights (gap 3).

Privileged actions in the identity provider and cloud consoles are logged to the SIEM. Directory privileged actions are logged on domain controllers and forwarded; ERP and HRIS admin actions are not forwarded.
The identity provider locks accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts and applies smart lockout to password spraying.
Device management locks laptops and desktops after 15 minutes idle and tablets after 5 minutes. Counter and dispatch PCs lock after 10 minutes.
Suite and identity provider sessions end after 12 hours or at risk events; cloud console sessions after 1 hour.

Remote access to internal systems is through the identity provider and device-checked VPN. Gaps: Fabrication machine vendors use an always-on remote access tool outside the VPN; the seller's IT provider reaches the Home Services North server directly.
evidence: VPN configuration; P07 remote access inventory

implementation_statement: VPN sessions are logged and sent to the SIEM. The plant vendor tool and the North connections are not monitored.
Corporate Wi-Fi uses enterprise authentication with device certificates at 8 of 9 sites; guest Wi-Fi is internet-only. Home Services North still uses a shared Wi-Fi key (moves with integration).

Laptops, desktops, and tablets are enrolled in device management with encryption and remote wipe. Warehouse scanners are managed by the scanner management server without encryption policy; 38 North laptops are unmanaged.

Personal phones may reach email and files only through the managed app with data protection. Personal computers are blocked by conditional access for integrated users; Home Services North users still use personal email for some work.

Sharing of Restricted data with outside parties (lenders, bank partner, sponsor, acquirers) needs data-owner approval under POL-04. Data room sharing is controlled; email sharing of HR and Finance files to outside addresses is not blocked.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 and POL-01 (approved 2026-09-22).

All employees complete annual training (96% in 2025) and quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 9.4%). Gaps: technicians and warehouse staff without email accounts get no simulations; Home Services North staff have had no group training.
Annual training includes insider threat indicators and how to report concerns.
Treasury and payables staff receive payment fraud training each year. Subsidiary staff who handle vendor changes locally (Home Services North office) have not.
Security staff complete role-based training; benefits staff have HIPAA training from the TPA's course only; directory administrators have had no privileged-access training.
Logging requirements are in POL-03; the logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) is in draft (P06).

Event types are defined for identity, suite, EDR, firewall, directory, and cloud sources. Gaps: HQ file servers, the plant network, Home Services North, the ERP, the HRIS, and the subsidiary SaaS systems (SYS-12 to SYS-14) send no logs (gap 8).
evidence: SIEM source list; P07 AU-2 results

implementation_statement: Collected records include time, source, user, action, and outcome; the MSSP normalizes fields.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews alerts 24x7; the security team reviews a weekly privileged-activity report. No review covers loan servicing exports or access to the benefits site.
evidence: MSSP monthly reports; weekly review tickets

implementation_statement: The MSSP correlates sources automatically in its SIEM platform.
Cloud logs go to a write-once bucket in the security and log archive account; SIEM data is read-only to group staff.
SIEM keeps 1 year searchable; the log archive keeps 3 years. Plan audit records needed for the HIPAA 6-year documentation rule are not identified.
Logging is enabled on all cloud accounts, the identity provider, the suite, domain controllers, and endpoints. Not enabled or not forwarded on the sources listed under AU-2.

The co-sourced internal audit firm assessed 36 controls from 2026-08-17 to 2026-09-04 (P07). It reports to the audit committee and does not operate any assessed control. The assessment also meets the sponsor's annual independent assessment requirement.

Interconnections with the banks, the bank partner (from 2027), the TPA, and the payroll provider have agreements. The machine vendors' remote connections and the seller's IT provider at Home Services North have no written terms.
Weaknesses are tracked in the POA&M (P07) with owners and dates and reported to the audit committee quarterly from 2026-09.
The CFO (system owner) accepted continued operation of the SCSP on 2026-09-22 with POA&M conditions; the CEO approved the High-risk treatment plans.
Continuous monitoring covers EDR, identity, cloud posture, and quarterly scans of HQ and the cloud. Branches, shops, and the plant are not scanned, and metrics are not yet reported monthly.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring (not in the Moderate baseline) because Finance needs annual penetration testing (16 CFR 314.4(d)(2)(i)). An external penetration test was done in 2025-11; the 2026 test (internal and external, including the directory) is booked for 2026-11.
Configuration requirements are in POL-01; the configuration standard (STD-01) is in draft.
Baselines exist for cloud images and the laptop image. There are none for servers, network devices, plant systems, or SaaS tenants.

Changes to the cloud, firewall, and identity provider go through tickets with peer approval. Directory, ERP configuration, and integration service changes are not consistently ticketed (P07: 7 of 25 changes lacked approval).
Security impact is considered for cloud changes. New SaaS features (for example AI features) were turned on without an impact analysis (P10).
Cloud guardrails block public storage and unencrypted volumes. Server and endpoint settings are not checked against benchmarks; P07 found 4 of 10 sampled servers with legacy protocols enabled.
Unneeded services are disabled on cloud images. The plant controllers and the HQ print server run legacy services.

The asset inventory comes from device management, EDR, and the cloud. Gaps: plant floor devices, warehouse scanners, Home Services North devices, and network gear are not in it; the SaaS inventory lists 64 applications against 112 found in expense reports.
Inventory updates automatically for managed endpoints and cloud resources; acquisitions and plant equipment are updated by hand.
Standard users cannot install software on managed laptops and desktops; requests go through the service desk catalog.
A data map showing where Finance customer information, plan PHI, employee SSNs, and deal information are stored is planned for 2026-12-31.
Contingency requirements are in POL-03; the contingency and recovery standard (STD-07) is in draft.

A cloud recovery plan exists (2025). There is no group contingency plan that covers the directory, HQ servers, the plant, Home Services North, and subsidiary workarounds; this BIA (P05) supplies the inputs.
Recovery plans are coordinated with the loan servicing and ERP vendors through their SOC 2 commitments; not with the distribution system vendor, whose RTO does not meet the BIA.
Recovery role training for IT and subsidiary leads is planned with the 2027 Q1 exercise.
The cloud workloads were restore-tested in 2026-03 (SFTP, integration service, warehouse). The directory, HQ file and scanner servers, and the plant server have never been tested (gap 7).
Cloud backups go to a separate backup account in a second region. HQ server backups go to a NAS in the same server room; the plant backup is a removable drive in the plant office.
Cloud workloads can be rebuilt in the second region. HQ servers and the plant server have no alternate site.
HQ and the distribution center have dual ISPs; branches and shops have cellular failover; the plant has a single ISP.
Cloud workloads: daily, encrypted, write-once 35 days, separate credentials. Suite: daily third-party backup. HQ servers: nightly to the HQ NAS. Plant server: weekly removable drive.
Backup integrity is tested for cloud workloads (2026-03); not for HQ or plant backups.
Recovery procedures exist for cloud workloads. There is no directory forest recovery procedure and no plant recovery procedure.
Identification and authentication requirements are in POL-02 and the authenticator standard (STD-06).
Every integrated user has a unique account. Gaps: 3 shared counter accounts at Branch 2 (P07) and local accounts in Home Services North's field-service product.
MFA (push with number matching) is required for all privileged accounts in the identity provider and cloud. Directory administration on domain controllers does not require MFA.
evidence: Conditional access policy; P07 sign-in tests

implementation_statement: MFA is required for all integrated users of SaaS systems. Home Services North and the plant vendor tool are outside it.

Push MFA with number matching resists simple replay but not adversary-in-the-middle phishing; phishing-resistant keys for administrators and payment, HR, benefits, and Finance staff are due 2027-03-31.
Identifiers come from the HRIS employee number and are not reused.

Passwords: 14 characters minimum with a banned list in the identity provider. Gaps: 23 directory service accounts with non-expiring passwords; the ACH signing service account password is stored in an IT runbook (P07; P01 R-050).
Contractor portal users (Supply customers) and the bank partner's future reviewers authenticate through vendor-managed accounts without MFA.
POL-03 (2024) was revised and approved 2026-09-22; it now names subsidiary roles and the plan PHI breach procedure.
Incident team training happened once (2024). Subsidiary Presidents and the Benefits Manager have had none.
One tabletop (2024, holding company only). Group tabletops for both P08 incident types are scheduled for 2026-11-18 and 2027-02-17.
The MSSP isolates hosts and escalates within 30 minutes; the security team runs response. P08 runbooks (2026-09-22) add crisis management, legal, and subsidiary steps.
Incidents are tracked in the service desk incident queue and the MSSP case system (41 security incidents in the 12 months to 2026-06-30).
Reporting duties are in the P08 notification matrix. Before 2026-09 there was no procedure for FTC notice or plan breach notice.
Incident response support comes from the MSSP and the cyber insurer's panel (counsel and forensics).
The 2024 plan covered the holding company only. P08 replaces it with two runbooks; subsidiary annexes are due 2026-12-31.
Remote maintenance by machine vendors uses an always-on remote access tool with shared credentials and no session logging (gap 9).
Retired drives from HQ are destroyed with certificates. Subsidiary sites ship devices to HQ without tracking (P07: 2 of 10 sampled retirements had no certificate).
Badge access protects the HQ server room and network closets at HQ and the distribution center. Shop and plant closets use keys.
Planning and policy governance is in POL-01 4.6 and 4.7 (review cycle and exceptions).
This SSP, approved 2026-09-22 by the CFO, documents the SCSP.
Rules of behavior are in POL-05; acknowledgments are collected at hire. Annual re-acknowledgment starts 2026-10.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring (not in the Moderate baseline) for group governance. The program is documented in POL-01 to POL-05, the standards index, and this SSP. The Finance supplement and plan security procedures are due 2026-12-31.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The vCISO leads strategy; the Security Manager is the written Qualified Individual for Finance (2025) and the plan's HIPAA Security Official (designated 2026-09-22).

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The risk appetite was rewritten with measures and approved by the board on 2026-09-22 (P01). Subsidiary Presidents now take part in a monthly cyber risk forum from 2026-10.
Background checks are done for all hires; enhanced checks for treasury, Finance, IT, and benefits roles.
Termination steps are in the HRIS workflow. Subsidiary managers report departures late (P07: 7 of 25 sampled terminations disabled after the last day; 2 still active in subsidiary SaaS).
Transfers between subsidiaries trigger a ticket, but prior access is not removed (P07: 6 of 25).
Contracts with the MSSP, TPA, and payroll provider include security terms. Machine vendors and the seller's IT provider have none.
Sanctions are in POL-01 4.8 and the HR discipline procedure; plan PHI violations are also logged by the plan's Privacy Official.
The SCSP is categorized Moderate (section 6 of the SSP), from the BIA (P05).
The 2026 group risk assessment (P01, 52 risks) uses NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 and covers Finance customer information and plan ePHI. Approved 2026-09-22.
Supply chain risk is assessed for critical vendors at onboarding; only 8 of 22 critical vendors have a current review.
Quarterly authenticated scans of HQ and the cloud; branches, shops, and the plant are not scanned. 18% of critical findings in 2026 H1 missed the 30-day target (P07).
Risk responses are recorded in P01 with owners and dates and tracked in the POA&M.
Security terms are in new SaaS and IT contracts since 2025. Subsidiary purchases (the recruiting software, the AI voice agent) bypassed procurement review.

External services are listed in the vendor register (about 160 vendors; 22 critical). SOC 2 reports are reviewed for 8 critical vendors (P09). The intercompany services agreement now includes a security schedule protecting Finance (signed 2026-09-22).
evidence: Vendor register; P09 reviews; intercompany agreement

implementation_statement: Two machine controllers run an unsupported embedded Windows version; the vendor supports them only on that version. Compensating controls (segmentation, remote access through the broker) are planned (gap 9).
Boundary protection at site firewalls and the cloud hub. Gaps: flat plant network; Home Services North connects to the internet only through its own firewall with no group policy.

control_name: Deny by Default ,  Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: Cloud hub and HQ firewall deny by default. Branch, shop, and plant firewalls still have broad outbound rules.
TLS 1.2 or higher for all SaaS and portal traffic; SFTP and VPN for bank files and site traffic.
Cloud keys are company-managed in the key service; backup keys are separate.
Encryption uses validated algorithms provided by the platforms.
Encryption at rest on SaaS, cloud storage, and managed laptops. Gaps: HQ file servers and the HQ NAS are not encrypted; warehouse scanners and the 38 North laptops are not.
Endpoints patch automatically; servers monthly. 18% of critical findings missed the 30-day target in 2026 H1; plant controllers cannot be patched.
EDR on all managed laptops, desktops, and servers. Not on the 38 North laptops, the warehouse scanners, or plant controllers.
24x7 MSSP monitoring of the sources in AU-2. No egress anomaly alerting on the file servers or the reporting warehouse.
The security team tracks vendor advisories and the known exploited vulnerabilities list weekly.
SaaS vendors protect record integrity. The ACH files on the SFTP server are not integrity-checked between creation and upload (P01 R-050).
A group retention schedule is planned for 2026-12-31. Finance keeps declined-applicant files and ACH files indefinitely today (gap 13).
A supply chain risk management plan is planned as part of the vendor risk standard (STD-03), due 2026-12-31.
Security terms and tiering exist for new IT contracts; subsidiary-led purchases bypass them.
8 of 22 critical vendors had a documented SOC 2 review by 2026-09 (P09).
Breach notice terms are in 12 of 22 critical vendor contracts; the TPA and PBM BAAs allow 60 days for breach notice.
